jobs.title: Packaging Lead Engineer
jobs.description:
Packaging Lead Engineer

In this role you will be responsible for setting up the enterprise packaging strategy and technology roadmap while leading a group of engineers.

Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive process standards and documentation to support all end-to-end packaging business and engineering workflows.

Establish packaging standards and lead execution of automation, returnable, and expendable plans while setting the standard on how Autoliv will achieve cost, quality, and sustainability goals. Assign workload to a team of engineers for new launch.

Should you be interested in overseeing these tasks and aiming for enhanced performance standards, your role will involve :

What you'll do

• Establish and maintain packaging standards for automation, returnable, and expendable execution; publish controlled specifications and playbooks

• Lead governance for exceptions/waivers; chair the standards review board and manage change control (ECO/ECN)

• Define common footprints and automation execution standards; align with safety/quality and sustainability requirements.

• Own enterprise packaging data architecture and tools (spec/PFEP, cartonization, labeling, image vaults): governance, permissions, and data-quality SLAs.

• Standardize master data (part-to-pack links, dunnage IDs, test results, sustainability attributes) and audit routines; lead training and adoption.

• Select/administer cartonization and labeling systems (GS1/AIAG compliant), including template libraries and formal change control.

• Set/enforce ID standards (serialization, barcode/QR/RFID), labeling, and traceability checkpoints (ship/receive scans, gate checks).

• Own the portfolio/roadmap for packaging materials, formats, and automation; prioritize pilots with success criteria and scale proven solutions.

• Conduct market/technology scouting; partner with suppliers/startups to mature innovations into standards.

• Develop KPIs/dashboards; monitor compliance and drive corrective actions with site leaders.

• Mentor regional teams; build capability via training, playbooks, and office hours

• Lead and set workload for a team of packaging engineers for new model launch and serialization projects

What is required

• BS in Packaging Engineering (preferred) or ME/IE

• 7–10+ years in packaging or logistics engineering, including multi-site standards/systems ownership in automotive/Tier-1 or similar high-volume manufacturing.

• Hands-on with PFEP/spec databases, cartonization (TOPS/Cape or WMS-native), labeling, and GS1/AIAG compliance.

• Experience integrating packaging data with ERP/PLM/WMS (e.g., SAP/Oracle; Teamcenter/Windchill); strong Excel/BI; familiarity with APIs/MDM concepts.

• Working knowledge of ISTA/ASTM transit testing, load-securement, and sustainability/EPR considerations.

• CAD & Packaging: SolidWorks/NX/CATIA; ArtiosCAD for corrugated/dunnage; read drawings, GD&T, basic tolerance stacks.

What’s in it for you

• Attractive compensation package

• Recognition awards, company events, family events, university discount options and many more perks.

• Gender Pay Equality

Equal opportunity employer

Autoliv is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Autoliv does not discriminate in any aspect of employment based on race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, gender, sexual orientation, gender identify and/or expression, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local employment discrimination laws where Autoliv does business.

Job Description

Packaging Engineer – Factory Zero

Onsite: This role is categorized as onsite. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to our Detroit/Hamtramck plant location

Sponsorship: GM DOES NOT PROVIDE IMMIGRATION-RELATED SPONSORSHIP FOR THIS ROLE. DO NOT APPLY FOR THIS ROLE IF YOU WILL NEED GM IMMIGRATION SPONSORSHIP (e.g., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT, etc.) NOW OR IN THE FUTURE.

The Role

The Packaging Engineer designs, tests, and implements packaging designs that are an integral part of the Automotive Aftermarket Product Development process. They also review and improve existing packaging designs.

Experienced level professional, requiring independent judgment and decision-making on significant matters as well as experience and or specialized training typically obtained through a specialized course of academic instruction.

Demonstrates very good understanding of the processes and procedures relevant to own work area with the ability to exercise decision-making skills sufficient to identify and propose solutions to leadership. Understands different areas of their function and how the operations of their area relate to others. Identifies and corrects non-routine problems in existing systems and processes through independent judgment. Independently identifies and applies appropriate company policies and procedures to resolve a variety of issues.

Works under general supervision with limited guidance and direction. Determines an appropriate course of action within broad guidelines and can handle nearly every standard or typical request independently. Exercises judgement within defined procedures and practices to determine appropriate action. Applies learned techniques to drive the solution to a problem, which typically will involve coordinating and integrating efforts of a diverse team of colleagues.

Engages in daily interactions with subordinates and/or peers from other functional groups. These interactions typically involve the exchange or presentation of information. Required to collaborate with team members 1-2 levels above. Adapts communication style to reach agreement in own area in situations of moderate complexity, demonstrates flexibility and ability to compromise.

Handles a range of moderate scope problems that are frequently routine but may vary, requiring analysis of various factors. Follows through on difficult situations and is expected to see through resolution. Proposes new initiatives and delivers solutions, driving cross team efforts. Recommends opportunities for process improvement to leadership & proactively anticipates needs within own area. Employee’s impact is typically within their immediate work area and occasionally across their function.

What You'll Do

(Responsibilities):

• Handles the complete packaging development process, including the creation of packaging designs, prototype development, and performance testing
• Fixes new and existing packaging problems involving designs, materials, processes and provides creative, timely, and cost-effective solutions
• Analyzes engineering drawings and specifications of product to resolve physical characteristics of item, special handling, environmental and safety requirements, and types of materials required for packaging
• Establishes standards and guidelines for supplier evaluation. Evaluates and selects packaging suppliers/vendors; periodically conducts vendor reviews
• Handles multiple projects simultaneously
• Works closely with global suppliers, engineering, product management, operations, and sourcing
• Manage daily ASRS operations by reviewing shift issues and following up on throughput, system faults, and Viadat transport or label problems.
• Improve ASRS processes and standardized work to support reliable flow and FIFO across shifts.
• Review ASRS-related label and packaging changes; support supplier compliance, FZ labeling, and resolution of ASRS label non-conformance issues.
• Manage ASRS dunnage availability, returns, repair/rework, audits, and scrap or shipment coordination; assess packaging capacity, cost, and space needs.
• Participates in product introduction teams to deliver new products to market

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

• Minimum of 3 yrs of Manufacturing Plant floor experience
• Prior Packaging Engineering
• Understand automation process & packaging requirements for automation
• Excellent practical problem-solving and analytical skills
• The ability to design temporary packaging
• Familiarity with time studies with re-packing
• Familiar with packaging shake testing and how to optimize performance
• Familiar with Specialized packaging, focus on maximizing density while still protecting part (fit, form & function) and meeting ergonomic requirement
• Experience with MGO & SPPS systems
• LMS (Lean Manufacturing Systems)
• Familiar with GMS Container requirements and ready to lead for GSC
• Experience working with suppliers to correct nonconformances, such as shipping label errors
• Ability to work with expendable container group and help optimize part density, feedback on carton design and inclusion of die cut openings on any bulk cartons for enable part picking
• Ability to track and remedy nonconformances in a timely manner to closure
• Familiar with Engineering part cleanliness specifications and how to work with supplier to obtain clean containers as required
• Work with 3PL (3rd Party Logistics) with movement of containers
• Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment
• Ability to work independently
• Experience working with suppliers

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge

• Bachelor’s Degree
• Prior in Plant Packaging Experience
• Experience with packaging for hazardous materials
• Prior Group Leader experience
• ASRS experience

jobs.title: Mechanical / Packaging Design Release Engineer – 12V Component Shields
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description

Our Mission:
At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale

Role Overview

We are seeking a Mechanical / Packaging Design Release Engineer (DRE) to lead the design, packaging, release, and execution of shields and associated mechanical interfaces for 12V components for vehicle programs. This role is responsible for translating system and vehicle requirements into robust shield and package solutions for generators, inverters, converters, battery vent tubes, jump start nuts, and related 12V hardware that support performance, manufacturability, serviceability, quality, and program timing.

The ideal candidate brings strong mechanical engineering fundamentals, product development experience, and the ability to drive cross-functional alignment across electrical, mechanical, packaging, manufacturing, quality, purchasing, and supplier teams.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead design release responsibility for assigned 12V component shields and related mechanical hardware
• Own mechanical design and package integration for shields supporting generators, inverters, converters, battery vent tubes, jump start nuts, and related 12V hardware
• Develop and maintain component requirements, design concepts, packaging studies, and release documentation
• Ensure shield designs meet vehicle packaging, environmental, mounting, sealing, durability, service, thermal, and assembly requirements
• Create and review engineering drawings, specifications, BOMs, and engineering change documentation
• Drive package integration within the vehicle environment, including clearance management, attachment strategy, surrounding component interfaces, and issue resolution
• Work closely with electrical, systems, packaging, and vehicle integration teams to ensure shields for generators, inverters, converters, battery vent tubes, and jump start hardware are properly packaged and supported within the full vehicle architecture
• Support CAD reviews, tolerance studies, DFMEA, DVP&R development, and validation planning
• Collaborate with suppliers to review designs, resolve technical issues, and support sourcing and execution
• Support prototype and production builds, issue resolution, root cause investigations, and implementation of corrective actions
• Manage engineering changes and execute deliverables in support of program timing, cost, quality, and performance targets

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline
• Experience in mechanical design, packaging, or design release engineering for automotive components
• Strong understanding of mechanical design principles, packaging integration, materials, manufacturing processes, and assembly methods
• Experience supporting shielding, brackets, housings, and packaging interfaces for automotive applications, including generators, inverters, converters, vent systems, jump start hardware, or similar 12V components
• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and GD&T
• Experience using CAD tools for component design and package reviews
• Experience working in a cross-functional product development environment
• Strong problem-solving, communication, and project management skills
• Ability to manage multiple technical issues and priorities in a fast-paced program setting

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with generator, inverter, converter, battery vent tube, jump start hardware, or similar 12V component packaging
• Experience with shield design, underhood packaging, bracket and attachment strategy, or vehicle electrical power environments
• Familiarity with shield mounting strategies, structural supports, vent routing, thermal protection, serviceability, and environmental protection considerations
• Experience with DFMEA, DVP&R, tolerance analysis, and change management
• Experience supporting supplier technical reviews, validation, and launch execution
• Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

What Success Looks Like

• Shields for 12V components are released on time and meet package, interface, and program requirements
• Mechanical designs support robust installation, retention, serviceability, durability, and thermal protection in the vehicle environment
• Cross-functional package and interface issues are identified early and resolved effectively
• Supplier and engineering concerns are driven to closure with strong technical ownership
• Shield designs achieve quality, cost, manufacturability, and performance targets

Location: Hershey, PA preferred, open to remote

Up to 70% Travel

Why Hershey

At The Hershey Company, we make more moments of goodness through some of the world's most iconic brands, including Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat®, Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, Dot's Pretzels, Lesser Evil and more. Our team supports a global portfolio of over 90 brands, creating opportunities to shape strategies and drive impact across a breadth of businesses that few companies can offer. While many organizations focus on a handful of brands, Hershey provides exposure to a diverse portfolio of category-leading brands enjoyed by consumers around the world. What truly sets us apart is our legacy. Inspired by Milton Hershey's belief that business should create opportunity for others, we have been making a positive impact for more than a century through our commitment to communities, philanthropy, and our longstanding partnership with Milton Hershey School. When you join Hershey, you become part of a company where purpose, growth, and making a difference are woven into how we do business every day.

How will you fit in the big picture?

The Staff Packaging Systems CI Engineer advances Hershey's multi-year Enterprise Continuous Improvement plan by identifying, developing, and implementing packaging-system improvements across the manufacturing network. Working independently and through cross-functional teams, you will lead complex initiatives from concept through sustainable plant handoff to improve cost, capacity, quality, safety, and supply continuity across Hershey's Global Confectionery and Salty businesses.

What will you do?

• Lead packaging-system continuous-improvement projects from opportunity identification and loss analysis through design, testing, installation, startup, commissioning, training, and performance stabilization.

• Develop project scopes, specifications, schedules, cost estimates, technical recommendations, and engineering deliverables for equipment selection, modifications, and layouts.

• Plan and execute proof-of-principle tests, designed experiments, scale-up activities, manufacturing trials, and feasibility assessments; translate results into practical technical and financial recommendations.

• Apply Lean, Six Sigma, TPM, packaging engineering, food science, and structured problem-solving methods to identify root causes and deliver sustainable solutions.

• Manage project cost, schedule, resources, risk, suppliers, and communication while partnering with Manufacturing, R&D, Engineering, Finance, Quality and Regulatory Compliance, Marketing, contractors, and equipment suppliers.

• Mentor engineers and technicians, provide clear technical documentation and training, and transfer improvements successfully to plant operations and maintenance teams.

Minimum Requirements

Education

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. A master's degree is welcome.

Experience

Minimum 5 years of relevant packaging-systems engineering, process design, project management, troubleshooting, or continuous-improvement experience in a manufacturing environment.

• Demonstrated ability to lead complex packaging or manufacturing improvement projects involving multiple unit operations and cross-functional stakeholders.

• Working knowledge of food-manufacturing systems, sanitary design, Good Manufacturing Practices, manufacturing validation, equipment suppliers, and plant implementation.

• Six Sigma Green Belt required; Six Sigma Black Belt preferred. Working knowledge of Lean manufacturing and TPM.

• Strong project planning, technical analysis, written and verbal communication, and Microsoft Office skills.

• Ability to travel up to 70%, support project work outside standard hours when needed, and work in manufacturing environments with regulated food allergens while following all site safety, food-safety, and allergen-control requirements.

Benefits and Perks

At Hershey, we offer competitive pay and a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, financial security, and life outside of work.

• Health & Wellbeing: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus wellness programs that support your physical and mental health begin on Day 1.

• Financial Security: Competitive pay, annual incentive opportunities, and a 401(k) with company match

• Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off, company holidays, and flexible ways of working where applicable

• Growth & Development: Career development programs, learning opportunities, and internal mobility

Benefits may vary based on role, location, and eligibility.

The Crafted Highlights

In the role of Sr. Strategic Project Engineer – Packaging in Milwaukee, WI, you will lead the development of long-range capital strategies for packaging and warehouse investments across North America. You will also lead front end project development, including business case analysis, alternative development and evaluation, concept development, and preliminary capital budgeting to ensure investments are technically sound, financially justified, and aligned with long-term business objectives.

• Establish scope, schedules, budgets, risk assessments, and business cases.

• Evaluate breakthrough programs, technologies, and process improvements.

• Provide technical leadership and packaging expertise.

• Assess emerging technologies and manufacturing approaches.

• You have 15+ years of relevant experience in capital project development, packaging engineering, manufacturing, supply chain operations, or the beverage industry.

• You possess a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.

• A Master's Degree or Postgraduate Degree is preferred.

• Experience developing large-scale strategic capital projects.

• Deep expertise in high-speed packaging systems, warehouse operations, industrial automation, and beverage manufacturing processes.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• You build relationships and collaborate to achieve desired outcomes.

• You act with integrity and accountability while driving results.

• You have a thirst for learning and are always looking for ways to learn and help others grow.

Beverage Bonuses

• Flexible work programs that support work-life balance including a hybrid work model of 4 days in the office.

• We care about our People and Planet and have challenged ourselves with stretch goals around our key priorities.

• We care about our communities and play our part to make a difference.

• Engagement with Employee Resource Groups.

• Participation in our Total Rewards program.

• On site Pub, access to brand clothing and swag, top events and free beer and beverages!

jobs.description:

This role will also assist in development of the multi-year equipment and capital strategy, development & standardization of manufacturing capabilities, leading continuous improvement efforts. This role leads cross-functional collaboration of internal and external partners, as well as headquarters and field stakeholders. Responsibilities Lead scope development, design recommendations, and vendor selection for Quaker packaging projects. Lead continuous improvement and lessons-learned practices. Support project execution for new capacity production lines and productivity projects at 4 Quaker facilities and occasionally contract manufacturers. Develop, manage, and execute equipment installation and start-up plans while supervising outside contractors and vendors. Support development and execution of the multi-year equipment strategy and commercialization for the Quaker fleet across 4 facilities. Support and lead cross-functional teams consisting of Headquarters, Operations, Maintenance, R&D, Equipment Vendors, Systems Integrators, External Engineering and Construction Contractors. Apply Engineering principles to problem solving and managing unexpected changes. Partner with OEMs to continuously improve equipment offerings, upgrades, training, and maintenance initiatives. Supports and encourages knowledge development of peers and partners. Develop into a subject matter expert (SME) for Quaker’s packaging equipment.

jobs.title: Packaging Engineer II, Amazon Leo
jobs.description:
LEO is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

The LEO team is looking for an exceptional Packaging Engineer to join our team and drive standardization and efficiency for product packaging in our supply chain. The Packaging Engineer will work closely with Engineering, Global Commodity Management, Supplier Quality Management, and Operations teams in the US and abroad to define efficient, robust, and standardized packaging for our products. You will be a critical escalation path for packaging issues and work closely with partner teams to ensure cross-functional collaboration is effective.

The team is looking for knowledge in the following fields of focus:
- Clean room compliant packaging
- Manufacturing kit packaging
- Manufacturing shadow form solutions
- Transportation solutions
- Labeling and barcoding (including developing supplier standards for labeling/barcoding)
- Proven strong organizational and problem-solving skills
- Demonstrated critical thinking capability
- Enthusiasm for getting “hands on” with your team in collaborative environments
- Ability to identify risks, develop clear mitigation plans, and communicate effectively to executive stakeholders while handling multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced rapidly evolving environment

Key job responsibilities
- Partner with operations to identify packaging/labeling defects impacting operations, including safety hazards created by packaging.
- Manage the development of Packaging concepts with Packaging Vendors and Component part Suppliers, ensuring material conformity and personnel safety.
- Plan and direct activities concerned with design and development of packaging. Analyze engineering drawings and specifications of product to determine physical characteristics of component, special handling and safety requirements.
- Create detailed packaging specifications for both components and manufacturing kits, including clean room compliance.
- Define standard labeling and barcoding specifications and partner with supply chain to drive adoption by suppliers. Monitor adherence to standards and drive corrective actions as appropriate.
- Scope new technology and/or opportunities in the packaging space.

jobs.title: System Development Engineer, Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI), RDPI Hardware Solutions
jobs.description:
Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI) Global Engineering is looking for a System Development Engineer (SysDE) to join our New Product Introduction (NPI) team. Our mission is to eliminate operational complexity at the source, ensuring every RDPI automation solution is designed for deployability, reliability, and maintainability from Day One.

As a SysDE II on the NPI team, you will work alongside Hardware Development programs from the Alpha phase to help shape controls and system design before solutions are built. Rather than fixing deployment and reliability problems in the field, you will help design them out — contributing to the automation, firmware, and integration decisions that determine how easily a solution scales across our global network. You are a builder who designs and delivers the controls software and tooling for the systems you support, works autonomously on well-scoped problems while seeking direction on ambiguous ones, and partners with Hardware Development, Technical Program Managers, and the Scale and AI teams to deliver solutions that deploy with minimal human intervention.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who thinks software-first and wants to grow in the software development craft. You will deepen core software engineering practices — modern languages, testing, CI/CD, and AI-native, agentic development — and apply them to industrial controls and hardware domains.

Key job responsibilities
- Contribute to NPI programs from Alpha through GA, helping influence controls and system design for deployability, reliability, and maintainability.
- Design and deliver standardized hardware/software interfaces and modular, reusable control patterns that reduce integration complexity, with guidance on the most ambiguous architectural decisions.
- Build and validate automation and commissioning frameworks (CI/CD for controls code, automated configuration validation, emulators) in partnership with the Scale team.
- Participate in reviews of architecture, design, and operations for your solutions, and incorporate feedback to raise the quality of your work.
- Partner with Hardware Development, TPMs, and the AI team to incorporate self-service deployment and predictive capabilities into solutions.
- Use AI-assisted and agentic development tools to increase the quality and velocity of your engineering work, and share what you learn with the team.
- Apply and help improve engineering and operational excellence standards, and mentor interns and junior engineers as you grow.

A day in the life
You work across industrial control platforms (Codesys, Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff) and the networked field devices, firmware, and cloud/WMS interfaces around them. You design and build the controls software for a solution, contribute reusable control patterns to our libraries, write and review structured-text and automation-tooling code, and work with Hardware to improve a system before it's built. You take part in design reviews that surface architectural and scalability risks early, and you prototype frameworks, emulators, automated validation, and CI/CD for controls code that become the foundation future solutions are built on. You lean on AI and agentic development tools throughout — generating, testing, and troubleshooting code — so you can focus your judgment on building solutions that are correct by design.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Packaging Product Stewardship - Nutrition - Columbus, OH
jobs.location: United States - Ohio - Columbus, United States of America
jobs.description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Program Manager, Packaging Product Stewardship

About Abbott

Working at Abbott

Our nutrition business develops science-based nutrition products for people of all ages, from helping babies and children grow to keeping adult bodies strong and active. Millions of people around the world count on our leading brands – including Similac®, PediaSure®, Pedialyte®, Ensure®, and Glucerna® – to help them get the nutrients they need to live their healthiest lives.

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

• Career development with an international company where you can grow the career you dream of.
• Employees can qualify for free medical coverage in our Health Investment Plan (HIP) PPO medical plan in the next calendar year.
• An excellent retirement savings plan with a high employer contribution
• Tuition reimbursement, the Freedom 2 Save student debt program, and FreeU education benefit - an affordable and convenient path to getting a bachelor’s degree.
• A company recognized as a great place to work in dozens of countries worldwide and named one of the most admired companies in the world by Fortune.
• A company that is recognized as one of the best big companies to work for as well as the best place to work for diversity, working mothers, female executives, and scientists.

The Opportunity

Our Columbus, Ohio location currently has an opportunity for a Program Manager within the Global Analytical & Food Safety (GAFS) organization, a key function within Abbott Nutrition Research & Development (R&D).

The Program Manager will lead Abbott Nutrition's Packaging Restricted Substance Management (RSM) Program and support strategic product stewardship initiatives that help ensure the safety, quality, regulatory compliance, and sustainability of Abbott Nutrition packaging worldwide.

This role serves as a key technical and program leader responsible for monitoring emerging packaging chemical regulations, assessing potential risks associated with substances of concern, and developing strategies to mitigate business impacts. The individual will partner closely with Packaging Engineering, Packaging R&D, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, Legal, Government Affairs, and external suppliers while collaborating across Abbott businesses to evaluate materials, support compliance programs, and drive risk-based decision making.

As part of the GA&FS organization, the Program Manager will apply scientific knowledge, regulatory insight, and strong project leadership skills to address evolving global requirements related to chemicals in packaging, packaging materials, and medical device components while supporting innovation and business continuity across Abbott Nutrition.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Lead Abbott Nutrition's Packaging Restricted Substance Management (RSM) Program and associated compliance activities.
• Monitor emerging chemical and product stewardship packaging requirements and evaluate potential impacts to Abbott Nutrition packaging and medical device components.
• Conduct risk assessments and provide recommendations regarding restricted substances, substances of concern, and evolving regulatory packaging requirements.
• Manage packaging restricted substance and material compliance data within internal systems and databases to support reporting, compliance, and business decision making.
• Lead annual packaging supplier surveillance and compliance verification programs to ensure adherence to Abbott requirements and applicable regulatory obligations.
• Evaluate new packaging materials, components, and supplier-submitted documentation for compliance with internal requirements and global regulatory requirements.
• Support material assessments for packaging, medical device components, and other materials used within Abbott Nutrition packaging and operations.
• Maintain compliance programs related to REACH, RoHS, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), Conflict Minerals, and other applicable global substance regulations.
• Collect, review, and assess supplier declarations, compliance certifications, technical dossiers, and supporting documentation for packaging.
• Provide technical support for internal stakeholders, customer inquiries, commercial opportunities, audits, and government affairs requests related to restricted substances and material compliance for packaging.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify, assess, and mitigate compliance and business continuity risks associated with emerging packaging regulatory requirements.
• Develop and communicate packaging regulatory intelligence, risk assessments, and compliance strategies to support informed business decisions.
• Prepare management updates, compliance reports, presentations, and recommendations for leadership and key stakeholders.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives related to product stewardship, restricted substance management, and material compliance processes.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE YOU’LL BRING

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Product Stewardship, Regulatory Affairs, Materials Science, Packaging Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemistry, or a related scientific discipline.
• Minimum 7 years of experience in product stewardship, regulatory affairs, material compliance, packaging compliance, environmental compliance, food safety, or a related technical field.
• Experience interpreting complex regulatory requirements and translating them into actionable business recommendations.
• Strong project management, leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
• Experience working collaboratively across multiple functions and organizational levels.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities and drive projects to successful completion.

Preferred Qualifications

• Advanced degree in a scientific, engineering, regulatory, or related discipline.
• Demonstrated knowledge of global chemical and product regulations, including REACH, RoHS, Conflict Minerals, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), and other substance restriction requirements.
• Experience supporting food, nutrition, medical device, pharmaceutical, consumer product, or packaging industries.
• Experience with food contact materials, packaging materials, and global food contact regulatory compliance requirements.
• Knowledge of U.S. FDA food contact regulations, EU food contact legislation, and other international food contact material frameworks.
• Experience evaluating packaging components, supplier compliance documentation, migration data, and material risk assessments.
• Experience leading supplier compliance, material stewardship, or restricted substance management programs.
• Familiarity with sustainability, circular economy, packaging stewardship, and chemicals management initiatives.
• Experience with regulatory intelligence, emerging issue monitoring, and risk assessment methodologies.

MISC:

• This is an on-site role - not a remote role.
• Sponsorship: we will not provide sponsorship of any kind for this role (including OPT).
• Relocation assistance is not offered for this role.

Apply Now

Learn more about our health and wellness benefits, which provide the security to help you and your family live full lives: www.abbottbenefits.com

Follow your career aspirations to Abbott for diverse opportunities with a company that can help you build your future and live your best life. Abbott is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to employee diversity.

Connect with us at www.abbott.com , on Facebook at www.facebook.com/Abbott and on Twitter @AbbottNews and @AbbottGlobal.
